nodes.label: §2 Stack (the same in every app)
nodes.text:
· Rust + Tauri 2 desktop shell (src-tauri), Windows first (NSIS per-user installer, WebView2).
· Engine in a pure-Rust crate (crates/core): all calculation lives there, with unit tests. The window only shows what the engine computes.
· UI: SolidJS + Vite + strict TypeScript in ui/src/*.tsx, built to ui/dist (embedded at compile time). State in ui/src/store.ts. Plain CSS with tokens (no CSS framework).
· Charts: Chart.js in the family chart style (see §7). An app may add its own SVG plot engine for publication graphs, but must keep this look.
· Spreadsheet formulas: the GridCraft crates (pinned git dependency, attribution in NOTICE) where the app needs them.
· No Python inside the apps (size and second runtime). The one exception is Datum Plot, which bundles its own Python (numpy, SciPy, matplotlib) for statistics and graphs; the decision is recorded in Plot's docs/MEMORY.md.
· Small, compact code that matches the surrounding style.

nodes.label: §4 Type
nodes.text:
· IBM Plex Sans for text, IBM Plex Mono for uppercase spaced labels, tabs, buttons, numbers and IDs (@fontsource, Latin subsets only, about 200 kB).
· Group captions, card headings and buttons: Plex Mono, 9.5–11 px, letter-spacing: .1em, uppercase.
· Body 12–13 px; page titles 23 px, 600–700 weight.
· Tables and grids: 12–13 px; numbers right-aligned.

nodes.label: §5 Logo and branding
nodes.text:
· Tile: 256×256 viewBox, a rounded square (x=8 y=8 w=240 h=240 rx=56), a white→accent-tint diagonal gradient, and a 4 px border in a light accent tint.
· Glyph: drawn in the accent with 11 px strokes, round caps. It may use one light tint fill (the --sky colour). It always has one amber #F2B233 diamond (the family mark).
· Files: ui/public/logo.svg (in the app) and docs/brand/datum-<app>-icon.svg (README). Windows icons are generated from it (npx tauri icon). Copies of every icon, and the family mark, are in this repo's brand/.
· The family mark ("Continuum", designed by the user): two concentric D's drawn as one continuous line, with the amber #F2B233 datum square where the line starts. Navy #0C1A2B (or light #E6EDF5) ink only, never an app colour, so it stays right however many apps the family has. Files, construction and rules: brand/BRAND.md (datum-logo.svg, datum-mark.svg, datum-icon.svg and light versions).
· Name: "Datum <App>" in Plex Sans 600. Tagline in the README.
· README: the logo, the name, a one-line tagline, shields.io badges (release, CI, downloads, license MIT, platform Windows 10/11, Rust, Tauri 2, SolidJS), then for-the-badge buttons (Download for Windows · What's new · Memory & roadmap), then a screenshot.

nodes.label: §6 Window layout
nodes.text:
· Title bar: quick access (save, undo, redo, print), document name, "Tell me what you want to do" (Ctrl+K), a Theme button (Auto/Light/Dark).
· Ribbon: a FILE button in the accent, then tabs. Groups have a mono uppercase caption. Big buttons have an icon above the label; split buttons have the command on top and the menu on the bottom ▾. Contextual tabs carry a small label above them. The ribbon never scrolls sideways: it tightens, then folds groups from the right (icons only).
· Left sidebar: icon + mono label per view, with Setup first. Groups are separated by rules.
· File page (backstage): a sidebar in the accent colour (Home, New, Open, Import, Save, Save As, Export, Print; Options and Updates at the bottom).
· Home: template tiles, recent files, a Roadmap tile, and the updates card. The card has Check again with a spinner and the time it checked, and the GitHub, Releases and Report an Issue buttons.
· Status bar: Ready, key facts, view switches, zoom.
· Options page: sections (General, Start-up and saving, New <documents>, Printing and branding, Updates). Each option has a name plus a one-line hint on the left and the control on the right.
· Help tab:
· Getting Started: written for people coming from other tools, in plain words;
· Glossary: plain-language terms, searchable;
· Shortcuts, Tell Me, What Is This Tool?;
· the GitHub links.
· ? help beside the tools: a small ? beside each ribbon group, page, panel and main dialog opens a card (what it is for, how to use it) from one HELP table in ui/src/help.tsx.

nodes.label: §7 Components
§8 Printing
nodes.text:
· File › Print (Ctrl+P) shows settings on the left and a live page preview on the right, for every view.
· The settings: paper, orientation, scaling or fit-to-pages, margins, page ranges, header and footer (left/centre/right) with codes and logos, legend, and view options.
· Pages are drawn as SVG at real size and printed with the WebView dialog ("Save as PDF").
· Report-type pages print as flowing documents with the header and footer on every page and page numbers.
· Reuse Plan's print.tsx (Frame, Slot, codes).

nodes.label: §9 Updates and releases
nodes.text:
· Updater: src-tauri/src/update.rs.
· Set REPO to the app's repo. It checks GitHub releases at start, and beta versions when turned on.
· It downloads the installer, checks SHA256SUMS and installs.
· The CHANGELOG section becomes the in-app "What's new".
· Versions: small numbered releases (0.1.0, 0.1.1, …), always three numbers (the updater compares three), consecutive with no jumped numbers.
· Release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml, windows-latest):
· builds the UI and the app and creates the tag;
· publishes Datum<App>-x.y.z-setup.exe + SHA256SUMS.txt.
· Run it with workflow_dispatch when tag pushes are blocked.
· CI (ci.yml, ubuntu): clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, npm run check:ui, the Playwright UI tests.
· Options and recovery files in the app's data folder (com.edgarmendonca.datum<app>).
· The family site rebuilds every day and on every push to DATUM, so a release appears there within a day (or at once, see MEMORY.md "Next").

nodes.label: §10 Docs in every repo
nodes.text:
· CLAUDE.md: read MEMORY first; update it at the end of every session; the user's preferences; the checks; the release steps.
· docs/MEMORY.md: product table, architecture (files), decisions (version | decision | why), roadmap (✅ 🔜 ⬜), session log, known limits, and the "How we work" workflow.
· CHANGELOG.md: ## x.y.z — date, a one-line summary, then bold sections in plain language for users. The site shows the last five sections.
· docs/site.json: the app's public summary, read by the family site at build time and by File › Roadmap in the app:
json
{
"id": "plan", "name": "Datum Plan", "accent": "#0B5CAD",
"logo": "docs/brand/datum-plan-icon.svg",
"tagline": "…", "for": "…",
"highlights": ["…"],
"screenshots": ["docs/images/gantt.png"],
"roadmap": [{ "v": "0.3.11", "title": "Fixes", "when": "Next", "items": ["…"] }]
}
when is one of Next, Soon, Later, Goal. Screenshots are 1440×900 PNGs in docs/images/.
· The brain: DATUM's brain/graph.json is generated from these files (node brain/brain.mjs); keep the MEMORY tables (Files, Decisions, Roadmap, Session log, How we work) in the same shape so it can read them.
· docs/PLAN-x.y.md: feedback → diagnosis → proposal → size → questions, written before any big release.
· NOTICE for third-party code and fonts; MIT license.

nodes.label: §11 How we work (from Datum Plan)
nodes.text:
· The user reviews a release and sends screenshots.
· Reproduce first.
· Big asks get a plan file and questions; build after the answers.
· Engine first (with a test), then the UI.
· Check every change in the real app (Xvfb screenshots).
· Add a UI test for every bug.
· Run all checks.
· Release.
· Report in plain language: what changed, what was checked, what is not done.

nodes.label: §12 Starting a new Datum app (checklist)
nodes.text:
· Create the repo Edgar-Mendonca/Datum-<Name> (MIT).
· Copy the skeleton from Datum Plan:
· the workspace Cargo.toml, crates/core (empty engine), src-tauri (main, update.rs, tauri.conf);
· ui/ (index.html with the icon sprite, styles.css, store.ts, ui.tsx, help.tsx, ribbon/backstage/options/print/roadmap patterns);
· package.json, .github/workflows, tests_ui/run.cjs, CLAUDE.md, NOTICE, LICENSE.
· Rename: product name, identifier, file extension, REPO in update.rs, installer name in release.yml.
· Apply the accent set from §3 and draw the logo per §5; copy the icon into DATUM brand/.
· Write docs/MEMORY.md and docs/PLAN-0.1.md (brainstorm and questions) before building features.
· Release 0.1.0 (shell, updater, Home, one working view) so the updater works from day one.
· Publish docs/site.json (§10) and add one line to DATUM's apps.json; the site picks the app up on its next build.

nodes.label: §13 Principles and public words
nodes.text:
Datum: free, open-source desktop tools for engineers, scientists, researchers and analysts. Small, fast apps that do serious technical work, written from scratch in Rust, with one look and one way of working. No accounts, no subscriptions, no telemetry: your files stay on your computer.
· Small and fast. Quick to install; opens in a moment; smooth with large files.
· Private. Files stay on the user's computer. The only network call is the update check.
· Built for real technical work. Each app has its own engine in a pure Rust crate, with tests.
· One design. The same window, ribbon, help, printing and updater in every app (§5–9).
· Small releases. One release is one small numbered version, shown in the in-app updater.
· Written down. Docs and memory are kept in every repo (§10).
· Free forever. MIT licence.
Rules for all public text (README, site, release notes, CHANGELOG):
· Describe what each app does and who it helps. Never name or compare with commercial products, and never say an app copies, clones or replaces one. Every Datum app has its own engine and its own design. (The family site leaves out any CHANGELOG or site.json line that names one, and lists it in the build log.)
· Say "free and open source (MIT)", "Windows first", "installs in seconds", "updates itself".
· Write plainly: short sentences, active verbs, no marketing filler. A visitor should know in ten seconds what each app is for.

nodes.label: Datum Plan
nodes.text:
Plan, schedule, track and report your projects: one small, fast app for Windows.

For: Project managers, planners, engineers and contractors.

Stack: Rust (engine + shell), Tauri 2, WebView2, SolidJS + Vite UI in strict TypeScript (TSX), plain CSS with light/dark tokens, Chart.js, IBM Plex fonts; Excel formulas from the GridCraft crates (pinned git dependency, see NOTICE)

nodes.label: Datum Plot
nodes.text:
Analyse data and make publication-ready graphs.

For: Scientists, researchers, lab teams and students.

Stack: Rust shell (src-tauri) + Rust project engine (crates/core), Tauri 2, WebView2, SolidJS + Vite UI in strict TypeScript, plain CSS tokens, IBM Plex. Python worker (py/) with numpy, SciPy and matplotlib for every calculation and every graph; the installer bundles embeddable CPython 3.13.

Project (name, info, tables, graphs, analyses, nextId, ui), Analysis (id, table, name, kind, sets, options JSON), GraphSettings.overlays (analysis ids drawn on the graph: curves, or brackets on column graphs), GraphSettings.column (scatter/bars/box/violin/mean/paired), GraphSettings.palette (scheme name or "#hex, …"), Info, Table (kind "xy" or "column"; a column table keeps the X column but never uses or shows it; Table::column(n); X column + sets; cols is the flat column list, column 0 = X; rows, rowTitles, excluded [row, col], style "r:c" → style string), DataSet (entry rep/msn/mesn, reps), Graph + GraphSettings (error, errorDir, points, line, cap, width/height mm, font, fontSize, boldTitles, style prism/frame, title, legend, x/y Axis, sets SetStyle). normalize, add_table, from_json (refuses newer formats).

nodes.label: doc.rs
nodes.text: Op: NewTable, Delete, Rename, Duplicate, Cells (col −1 = row title), Import (rows → new table + graph; titles from the first row; sets of reps), AddAnalysis (overlay → drawn on the table's graphs, joining lines off), SetAnalysis, Overlay, Sort (rows by a column, empty last, titles/exclusions/styles move), CopyLook (look of one graph onto others, keeping titles, axis titles and ranges, overlays, line), Paste (first row of words = titles; grows rows and data sets), Exclude, TableSet, SetDef (add/replace/remove a data set, remapping columns, exclusions and styles), Rows (insert/delete, remapping), Style, AddGraph, GraphSet, Info, ProjectName, Ui, Batch. number() parses 1,234.5 / −4 / 12% / 1e-3.

nodes.label: templates.rs
nodes.text: Blank XY, Growth curve, Standard curve (mean/SD/N), Dose-response (log X), Tensile test (modulus fit 0–0.003 + tensile analysis), Arrhenius (activation energy, log Y), Compare groups (column table, ANOVA + Tukey brackets), Weibull strength (column table, box plot, Weibull analysis), DSC peak (area above a straight baseline); list() gives tile pictures (column tables: the group means).

nodes.label: dump.rs

nodes.label: main.rs
nodes.text: Commands in the diagram plus result (an analysis via the Calc engine, cached), models, export_all (folder picker, every graph, unique file names), export_excel (save dialog → Python excel), new_table(kind) (column tables), graph requests carry overlays; copy_graph (PNG → Windows clipboard via tauri-plugin-clipboard-manager), copy_text, read_clipboard, import_file, restart_engine; Options (theme, autosave, beta, openLast, decimals, reps, entry, error, width, height, font, fontSize, style, dpi, paper, landscape, company, logo, styles = saved graph styles); new_project keeps a sample graph's x, y, line, error, overlays, points, column, sets, palette; new tables/graphs follow the options; recovery; recent files; open_url only for this repo.

nodes.label: py.rs
nodes.text: Finds Python (DATUM_PYTHON, the runtime pack, else python/python3); a reader thread lets requests time out (start 180 s, request 60 s → kill and report); restart(); and py/worker.py (bundled or the source tree), MPLCONFIGDIR in the app cache, CREATE_NO_WINDOW, restart once on failure, cache of the last 24 requests. Two workers (I3): Engine draws graphs, Calc runs results, models and Excel export, so a long fit never holds up drawing; both start in a thread at launch (Calc after Engine is ready); Restart Engine restarts both; emits engine with versions or the error.

nodes.label: update.rs

nodes.label: runtime.rs

Release Windows builds only; dev builds use the PATH Python. 1 test.

nodes.label: runtime.txt

nodes.label: analysis.py
nodes.text: Analyses: run(kind, table, sets, options) → {title, answer, tabs of formatted tables, checks, methods, legend, code, plots (small SVGs), curves (for graphs), cells (outliers)}. Kinds: describe, normality (Shapiro, D'Agostino, Anderson-Darling, Lilliefors + QQ), outliers (iterative Grubbs), linear (OLS/WLS via statsmodels, origin, polynomial, Deming with jackknife SEs, fit range, compare lines F tests, runs test, CI/PI bands, interpolation), fit (lmfit ExpressionModel, library or own equation, init/fixed, CIs, AICc, correlations, bands), arrhenius (ln k vs 1/T, Ea, A). g() formats numbers, pv() APA P values.

nodes.label: groups.py
nodes.text: Compare groups (B4–B8, B16, B23): column (values by row, for pairing), summary (values, or entered mean/SD/N), pairs_of; ttest (unpaired Welch/Student from stats, paired, ratio, one-sample; effect sizes; Shapiro and Brown-Forsythe checks), nonparam (Mann-Whitney + Hodges-Lehmann, Wilcoxon (approximate with ties, as R), KS, Kruskal-Wallis + Dunn (Bonferroni), Friedman), anova (ordinary, Welch/Brown-Forsythe via statsmodels anova_oneway, repeated measures with Geisser-Greenhouse; posthoc Tukey (scipy.stats.tukey_hsd), Dunnett (scipy.stats.dunnett), Holm-Šidák, Šidák, Bonferroni, LSD; trend; η², ω²), correlation (Pearson + Fisher-z CI, Spearman, Kendall, matrix), power (statsmodels power solvers, curve). Results carry brackets [set, set, P].

nodes.label: tools.py
nodes.text: Data tools and materials (A15, A18, D4, B14, B27, B29): transform (X/Y functions, baseline, normalise, replicates → mean/SD/N), check, frequency (common bins, histogram/QQ/ECDF plots), auc (trapezoid, baselines incl. a straight line, peaks; curves with fill), smooth (Savitzky-Golay, LOWESS, moving average; derivatives, cumulative integral), tensile (per specimen: modulus by least squares in a range or 10–40 % of UTS, offset yield, UTS, elongations, toughness; dashed offset line), weibull (MLE with Hessian CIs, median-rank regression, Weibull plot). Built-in data compiled by us from public sources, a reference for every value; never proprietary databases

Plan, memory and questions before any feature code; build 0.1.0 after the answers

nodes.label: Own SVG chart engine; Datum Plot's matplotlib renderer is not…
nodes.text:
Own SVG chart engine; Datum Plot's matplotlib renderer is not reused, but its graph-view patterns are (log/linear mapping, hover, crosshair, double-click zones, docked Format panel, export dialog, Copy Picture through Rust)

Why: Plot draws with Python, which Atlas does not have (PLAN §3).

nodes.label: Rust computes chart geometry (bubbles, hulls); the window owns…
nodes.text:
Rust computes chart geometry (bubbles, hulls); the window owns the view transform, ticks and labels

Why: Pan and zoom need no engine call per frame; values still come only from the engine.

nodes.label: Dependencies arrive with the release that needs them: Chart.js…
nodes.text:
Dependencies arrive with the release that needs them: Chart.js (radar/bars), GridCraft (expressions), calamine/rust_xlsxwriter (import/export)

Why: Keep 0.1.0 small and quick to build.

nodes.label: Database as reviewed JSON in data/, embedded with include_str!…
nodes.text:
Database as reviewed JSON in data/, embedded with include_str! and validated by cargo test; each material has a status (draft/checked)

Why: Readable diffs for every value and its source; honest drafts that tighten over releases.

nodes.label: Answers (PLAN-0.1 §10): name Datum Atlas; engineers and…
nodes.text:
Answers (PLAN-0.1 §10): name Datum Atlas; engineers and students; 100 materials; users add their own with a window explaining what is needed; eco audit and process selection before 1.0; earlier "material atlas" repo not used; references and sources as proposed; print in 0.1.0; whole UI laid out; brief's tabs incl. Home; Okabe-Ito families; classic look; °C and USD/kg; new violet logo; each app's memory in its own repo

Why: The user's answers, 2026-10-24.

nodes.label: Basic selection (limits, line, box, families, results) moved…
nodes.text:
Basic selection (limits, line, box, families, results) moved into 0.1.0; index builder and expressions become 0.2

Why: The user: "start with the basics: how the property charts are done, selection and so on".

nodes.label: Follow the established selection tool's workflow, never its…
nodes.text:
Follow the established selection tool's workflow, never its data, names, wording or artwork

Why: The user suggested copying it; the brief forbids proprietary data and naming other products. Functional workflow is fine.

nodes.label: Elastomers and foams are top-level families (own colour and…
nodes.text:
Elastomers and foams are top-level families (own colour and envelope)

Why: They sit apart on every chart.

nodes.label: Family envelopes are split into groups of nearby bubbles
nodes.text:
Family envelopes are split into groups of nearby bubbles

Why: One convex hull around a spread-out family (natural materials, foams) covered half the chart.

nodes.label: Click on a bubble shows a short datasheet beside the chart…
nodes.text:
Click on a bubble shows a short datasheet beside the chart; double-click opens the full one

Why: Keeps the chart in view while exploring; the brief's "click opens the datasheet".

nodes.label: UI tests run the real engine through examples/bridge.rs…
nodes.text:
UI tests run the real engine through examples/bridge.rs instead of a static fixture

Why: Dragging the line, limits and Add Material need real answers.

nodes.label: Ceramic, glass and stone strengths: tensile column holds the…
nodes.text:
Ceramic, glass and stone strengths: tensile column holds the flexural strength (noted on the datasheet); compressive strength added as its own property

Why: Ceramics have no yield strength; the tensile test is rarely done.

nodes.label: Answers to PLAN-0.1.1 §7: build §3; 22 goals (the screenshot…
nodes.text:
Answers to PLAN-0.1.1 §7: build §3; 22 goals (the screenshot showed 14, so 8 extras); goals set the line and suggest limits; a goal changes the open chart; check data now, metals first; no teaching mode

Why: The user's answers, 2026-10-25.

nodes.label: Goal limits are marked (Limit.goal) and replaced by the next…
nodes.text:
Goal limits are marked (Limit.goal) and replaced by the next goal; the user's own limits are never touched

Why: A goal must be easy to change without losing the user's work.

nodes.label: ? help beside the tools in every Datum app: a click opens a…
nodes.text:
? help beside the tools in every Datum app: a click opens a card saying what the tool is for and how to use it, from one HELP table

Why: The user, instead of a teaching mode: “we should do it in all of our applications”.

nodes.label: Data check cites only primary publishers (producers…
nodes.text:
Data check cites only primary publishers (producers, suppliers' own datasheets, universities, government), never aggregator sites (MatWeb, MakeItFrom, Total Materia, Wikipedia); a value is marked checked only if the datasheet's figure falls in our range, else the range is widened to include it

Why: Open sources only, and honest ✓ marks.

nodes.label: The check used the figures quoted by web search from each…
nodes.text:
The check used the figures quoted by web search from each datasheet (the build machine cannot open web pages); a second pass that opens each document is planned

Why: Recorded so nobody mistakes it for a table-level check.

nodes.label: Derived properties are computed by the engine at load, not…
nodes.text:
Derived properties are computed by the engine at load, not stored

Why: One source of truth; they follow corrections automatically.

nodes.label: Logo: violet log–log axes, a dotted selection line between two…
nodes.text:
Logo: violet log–log axes, a dotted selection line between two family envelopes (the upper one with a violet bubble), the amber diamond at the line's end

Why: The user asked for a better violet logo; it keeps FAMILY §5.

nodes.label: Session 1 (plan)
nodes.text:
· The user started Datum Atlas as the third Datum app: Violet accent, .datlas/.datdb, com.edgarmendonca.datumatlas, this repo for releases, no Python, data from public sources with a reference for every value. Asked for CLAUDE.md, this file, docs/PLAN-0.1.md and the brief's questions before building.
· Read Datum Plan (read-only): the brief, FAMILY.md, CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md, CHANGELOG.md, the reference code (styles, icon sprite, ribbon, backstage, print, selection/cells/fmt, update.rs, release and CI workflows, UI tests) and the draft logo.
· Read Datum Plot (read-only): CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md, PLAN-0.1, graph.tsx, format.tsx, print.tsx, py/datum/graph.py. Finding: Plot's graphs are drawn by matplotlib in Python, so only its window-side patterns carry over (PLAN §3).
· Wrote CLAUDE.md, this file and PLAN-0.1.md (16 questions). Copied the draft logo. No code yet. Waiting for the answers.
· Noticed in passing: Datum Plan's CHANGELOG.md has lost the ## x.y.z — headings of 0.3.7 to 0.3.3 (only " 2026-10-24" remains), so their notes cannot be found by version.

nodes.label: Session 2 (answers, 0.1.0)
nodes.text:
· Answers recorded in PLAN-0.1.md §10 (see decisions). Built 0.1.0:
· Engine: model, units, db (embedded data + checks), geometry (ellipses, rounded hulls, clusters), chart, select (stages, reasons, ranking, line values), doc, templates; 12 tests.
· Data: 100 materials (31 metals, 23 polymers, 8 elastomers, 15 ceramics and glasses, 7 composites, 6 foams, 10 natural), 13 properties each where known, 9 sources; all drafts.
· Shell: commands, user database My materials.datdb, options, recovery, updater for this repo.
· Window: chart view, Browse, Datasheet, Stages, Results, Add Material, Setup, Data, laid-out pages (Compare, Index, Report), ribbon with every planned command, File page, Print, Options, Help.
· New violet logo and Windows icons; README with screenshots; CHANGELOG.
· Released 0.1.0 with release.yml (workflow_dispatch): CI and Release green; installer 2.2 MB.
· Checked: Playwright with the real engine (30 checks); the real app under Xvfb (Home, "Hot, stiff and light", hover with the failure reason, dragging the line: chart stage 24 → 57).
· Fixed while testing: a click on a bubble under the selection line was swallowed by the line; one convex envelope per family covered half the chart (now groups); ρ shown as "P" in uppercase mono headings; symbols with underscores (K_Ic).

nodes.text:

nodes.label: Session 4 (answers, 0.1.1)
nodes.text:

· Engine: goals.rs (22 goals, apply), Op::Goal, derived properties, imperial units for the new units, bar charts (bands), index names with ½ ⅓ ⅔ ², templates from goals, checked-value rule; 16 tests.
· Window: goal list (with groups) and Why card, two-row chart toolbar, Setup goal list, Home tiles, Sources page, units everywhere (axes, ticks, tables, datasheet, limits, Add Material), bar charts, Copy Picture, label nudging, Tell Me finds goals and materials, ? help on the tools (help.tsx) and Help › What Is This Tool?.

· Not done: metals still draft: 1020, 1080, 304, 316, 430, grey iron, 1100, AZ91, Inconel 625, CoCr F75, zinc AG40A, lead, tin, tungsten (no primary datasheet found, or the datasheet disagreed with our range in a way that needs a closer look).
